name: pass1-brownfield-proposed
description: The anchor-rule discrimination fixture: one Accepted ADR carries a `present` violated boundary, a `present` claim naming a nonexistent component, and a `future` proposal — against a repo that has `inventory`+`pricing` but no `recommendations` and no `catalog`. Grades that the anchor rule yields three DISTINCT verdicts: violated / dangling-anchor / internally-sound. `test-files/expected-verdicts.json` is the grader-only oracle, excluded from `files[]`. Unresolvable cross-module imports in the slice are intentional static topology, not a fixture bug.
trap: The reviewer is likely to collapse two or three of these into one verdict: (a) mark the `recommendations` ownership claim `violated` (treating a missing COMPONENT the same as a missing MECHANISM) instead of `dangling-anchor`; (b) mark the `inventory` boundary `dangling-anchor` by anchoring on the dependency edge rather than the existing inventory service; (c) flag the `future` `catalog` proposal `violated`/`dangling-anchor` because catalog does not exist yet, instead of short-circuiting to internal-soundness on `future` tense; or (d) mis-tag the 'we will introduce' clause as `present` despite it overriding the Accepted default.

assertions.text: The `inventory` boundary claim (dimension 1, present) resolves its anchor to the EXISTING inventory service, selects reality mode, finds the forbidden import of pricing/schema, and is graded `violated` (P1).
The `recommendations` ownership claim (dimension 2, present) is graded `dangling-anchor` (P2) because no `recommendations` service exists in the repo — NOT `violated` and NOT `verified`.

The `catalog` proposal is tagged `tense: future` (the prospective 'will introduce / will read / will never import' wording overrides the Accepted default) and graded in internal-soundness mode as `internally-sound` — it names the one-way permitted dependency direction. If conjunction-split, every resulting catalog sub-claim is `future` + `internally-sound`; none is graded against the repo.
The `future` `catalog` proposal is NOT flagged `violated` or `dangling-anchor` even though the catalog service is absent from the repo — future tense short-circuits the anchor branch.
The three verdicts are DISTINCT (violated / dangling-anchor / internally-sound); the reviewer does not blend a missing component with a missing mechanism, nor a proposal with a violation.
Altitude — the `violated` finding rests on the static import/manifest of the inventory service, not on runtime or behavioral reasoning.
